_meta.title: RaceLab World Map of Competitive RC Racing — master taxonomy
_meta.purpose: Enumerate the full competitive RC racing taxonomy worldwide (chassis class x surface x power sub-class) and flag what RaceLab under-covers. in_racelab_coverage is judged against RaceLab's stated class-groups, NOT against extracted setup templates (only the Kyosho Inferno MP11 has a full template today; everything else is registry/category-stub).
_meta.coverage_note: RaceLab's chassis registry/category stubs cover ~16 categories. A class flagged in_racelab_coverage=true means RaceLab acknowledges the class-group; it does NOT mean a tuned KB/template exists. The setup-axis gaps (surface + power sub-class) are the bigger advice risk than the chassis-class gaps.

governing_body_glossary.IFMAR: International Federation of Model Auto Racing — world championships
governing_body_glossary.ROAR: Remotely Operated Auto Racing — North American sanctioning body
governing_body_glossary.EFRA: European Federation of Radio Operated Model Automobiles
governing_body_glossary.JMRCA: Japan Model Radio Control Association / Car
governing_body_glossary.ETS: Euro Touring Series (LRP/private series, on-road touring)
governing_body_glossary.EOS: Euro Offroad Series (private indoor carpet/astro offroad series)
governing_body_glossary.USVTA: United States Vintage Trans-Am (spec vintage touring series)
governing_body_glossary.WGTR: World GT-R rules (GT12 / WGT pan-car spec community)

disciplines.name: 1/8 nitro off-road buggy
disciplines.setup_relevance: The flagship outdoor class: long jumps and rough terrain make shock oil/piston, ride height, droop, diff oils (3-way) and tyre compound-vs-surface the dominant levers; engine clutch/needle tuning is a whole second domain. Setup swings hard with track moisture and time-of-day grip change.
disciplines.notes: RaceLab's deepest area — only fully-templated chassis (Kyosho Inferno MP11) lives here.

disciplines.name: 1/8 electric buggy (e-buggy)
power: brushless modified (no fixed turn cap, typ. 4-pole 2000-2100Kv on 4S)
disciplines.setup_relevance: Same chassis family as nitro 1/8 buggy but battery weight bias (lower/centred) and instant electric torque shift CG, diff and traction-roll tuning; no clutch/needle, so the tuning surface is purely chassis+drivetrain+tyre.
disciplines.notes: IFMAR added the inaugural 1/8 e-buggy World Championship for the 2025/26 cycle — a fast-growing class.

disciplines.name: 1/8 nitro truggy
disciplines.setup_relevance: Taller, heavier, wider than 1/8 buggy on the same platform; big tyres and high CG make anti-squat, sway bars and shock position the key stability levers. Less an IFMAR-title class, more a regional/national staple.

disciplines.name: 1/8 electric truggy (e-truggy)
disciplines.setup_relevance: Electric counterpart of nitro truggy; heavy battery + tall body amplifies traction roll, so sway-bar and droop tuning dominate. A real raced class at US club/regional level but absent from RaceLab.
disciplines.notes: FORGOTTEN: RaceLab lists nitro truggy + e-buggy but not e-truggy. Cheap to add — it reuses truggy chassis + e-buggy power vocabulary.

disciplines.name: 1/8 IC GT (on-road GT)
disciplines.setup_relevance: Heavy GT-bodied on-road car: aero/downforce, foam-vs-rubber tyre choice, camber/toe and high-speed stability dominate; near-zero suspension travel vs off-road. eGT now an IFMAR World Championship class (inaugural 2025, Peru).
disciplines.notes: RaceLab covers the nitro/IC GT; the new electric eGT sub-variant should be flagged explicitly.

disciplines.name: 1/10 200mm nitro on-road touring
disciplines.setup_relevance: 200mm-bodied nitro sedan: tyre additive/compound, ride height, roll centre and clutch/needle. IFMAR 1/10 Nitro Touring World Championship class (2025 Costa Rica).

disciplines.name: 1/10 electric touring car (TC) — modified
disciplines.setup_relevance: The blue-riband on-road class: shimmed droop, roll centres, ARBs, diff/spool, camber/toe and tyre additive on glue-grip surfaces. Boosted/timing ESCs add motor-tuning as a lever. IFMAR ETC World Championship (2025 California).
disciplines.notes: RaceLab says 'touring (modified + stock)'. Carpet vs asphalt is a major un-modeled surface split inside this one class.

disciplines.name: 1/10 electric touring car (TC) — stock / spec (17.5T blinky)
disciplines.setup_relevance: Same chassis as modified TC but locked 17.5T blinky power flattens the powerband, so corner-speed/rotation and tyre management drive the setup far more than power delivery; gearing and rollout become a precise lever.
disciplines.notes: RaceLab acknowledges stock TC but the stock-vs-mod setup DIVERGENCE (power-down vs corner-speed) is the kind of thing advice must respect; verify it is modeled, not just labeled.

disciplines.name: 1/12 electric pan car (modified + stock)
disciplines.setup_relevance: Ultra-low single-cell pan car: side-spring/tube tuning, front end (kingpin/coil), ride height in tenths of a mm, and foam tyre diameter/compound. Tiny changes = big swings. IFMAR 1/12 Worlds (2025 China).
disciplines.notes: Stock vs modified 1/12 are distinct race classes; flag both.

disciplines.name: 1/10 World GT / GT12 (WGT pan car)
disciplines.setup_relevance: GT-bodied pan car (GT12 ~750g min, WGT ~1025g/200mm class): a separate body/aero and weight package from 1/12 track pan cars, with its own spring/ride-height window. Hugely popular UK/EU club racing.
disciplines.notes: FORGOTTEN: distinct from RaceLab's '1/12 electric pan'. GT12 and World GT are big grassroots pan classes with their own bodies, weights and setup windows.

disciplines.name: 1/10 Formula 1 (F1 pan car)
disciplines.setup_relevance: Open-wheel narrow-front pan car: front kingpin/caster, rear pod tuning, ride height and a narrow rubber-tyre window; extremely sensitive to track grip and tweak. 21.5T is the common spec.

disciplines.name: 1/10 2WD electric off-road buggy
disciplines.setup_relevance: The premier 1/10 off-road class: rear-drive means weight transfer, slipper, gull-wing/laydown trans, and tyre-vs-surface dominate; setup is radically different on loose dirt vs grippy astro/carpet. Both 2WD Worlds (2025 Australia) and stock/mod splits.
disciplines.notes: Surface axis (dirt vs clay vs carpet/astro) is THE differentiator here and is the most setup-relevant gap to model.

disciplines.name: 1/10 4WD electric off-road buggy
disciplines.setup_relevance: 4WD adds front/centre/rear diff tuning and a more planted-but-push-prone balance; sway bars and diff oils are key. Stock vs modified and dirt vs astro both swing setup. Worlds run alongside 2WD.

disciplines.name: 1/10 stadium truck (2WD)
disciplines.setup_relevance: 2WD truck on buggy-derived chassis with big tyres/high CG: anti-squat, rear toe and tyre choice control wheelspin and stability. Strong US class, weaker in EU.

disciplines.name: 1/10 short course truck (2WD/4WD)
disciplines.setup_relevance: Heavy SCORE-style body, lots of body roll and contact; sway bars, shock geometry and tyre wear dominate. Distinct 2WD and 4WD short course classes exist.
disciplines.notes: RaceLab lists 'short course truck' generically — verify 2WD vs 4WD SCT are both representable; 4WD SCT is a separate setup problem.

disciplines.name: 1/5 large scale (1/5 & 1/6)
disciplines.setup_relevance: Heavy gas cars (FG/Smartech-style): real-car-like geometry, big shocks, brake balance and engine/clutch tuning. On-road LS and off-road LS are separate; 1/6 scale trucks sit adjacent.
disciplines.notes: RaceLab says '1/5 large scale'; 1/6 scale and the on-road-vs-off-road LS split are adjacent and under-specified.

disciplines.name: Competition rock crawler (comp crawler)
disciplines.setup_relevance: Not speed racing — a points/gate discipline: CG height, link geometry, droop, tyre foam compound and weight placement for grip and balance on vertical terrain. Totally different 'setup' vocabulary from racing classes.
disciplines.notes: Distinct from scale/trail crawling (bashing). RaceLab covers comp crawler.

disciplines.name: Monster truck racing/freestyle (Solid Axle Monster Truck, SAMT)
disciplines.setup_relevance: Solid-axle leaf/link trucks for racing + freestyle: shock/spring for big landings, steering and CG. RaceLab has a monster_truck category stub. Niche racing, large basher overlap.
disciplines.notes: RaceLab has a monster_truck category stub; competitive SAMT racing is small but real.

disciplines.name: Dirt oval — Sprint car (410/360 wing sprint)
surface: clay/dirt oval (high-bite to dry-slick, changes through a session)
disciplines.setup_relevance: Buggy-converted left-turn-only car with big rear wing and offset/stagger: left-side weight bias, rear stagger, tyre stagger and wing angle are the dominant levers — a setup language RaceLab does not speak at all.
disciplines.notes: FORGOTTEN (whole sub-domain): oval cars use weight-bias/stagger/wedge setup that has no analog in RaceLab's symmetric-track classes.

disciplines.name: Dirt oval — Late Model
disciplines.setup_relevance: Wide late-model body on buggy-derived chassis; more aero/sail-panel side-bite than sprint, with the same left-weight/stagger/wedge tuning. Faster than modifieds.
disciplines.notes: FORGOTTEN: distinct oval body/aero class.

disciplines.name: Dirt oval — Modified (Midwest Mod / East-coast Mod / Dirt-Mod)
disciplines.setup_relevance: Open-wheel/open-cockpit oval modified; lighter than late model, very stagger- and wedge-sensitive. Several regional sub-flavors (MWM vs ECM) with different body rules.
disciplines.notes: FORGOTTEN.

disciplines.name: Dirt oval — Midget / EDM / Legends / Street Stock (Mudboss)
disciplines.setup_relevance: Entry/spec oval classes — notably the SCT-based Mudboss (spec short-course-on-oval) which is one of the most popular grassroots oval classes; spec tyre + spec motor + weight rules make chassis tweak/wedge the only real lever.
disciplines.notes: FORGOTTEN: Mudboss especially is a massive spec oval class RaceLab ignores.

disciplines.name: Paved / carpet oval (asphalt oval, legends-on-asphalt)
disciplines.setup_relevance: On-road pan/touring car on a banked or flat left-turn oval: extreme left-side weight bias, tyre stagger, sway-bar and ride-height for the corners only. Different from dirt oval (grip is consistent, banking matters).
disciplines.notes: FORGOTTEN: the on-road oval branch (banking + stagger) is its own setup discipline.

disciplines.name: M-chassis / mini touring (1/10 mini)
disciplines.setup_relevance: Short-wheelbase narrow mini hatch (e.g. Mini Cooper bodies): high CG and narrow track make weight, droop and a small spec-tyre window the levers; very popular budget club class in EU/Asia.
disciplines.notes: FORGOTTEN: a big grassroots class, distinct geometry from full TC.

disciplines.name: Vintage / classic touring (USVTA Trans-Am, vintage off-road)
disciplines.setup_relevance: Spec foam-tyre + spec body + spec motor vintage classes: with everything locked, weight, ride height and shock/spring are the only levers. Hugely popular spec entry class in the US.
disciplines.notes: FORGOTTEN: USVTA is one of the largest spec on-road communities in North America.

disciplines.name: RWD competitive drift (1/10)
disciplines.setup_relevance: Judged (not raced) discipline: counter-steer geometry, Ackermann, gyro gain, motor/tyre for controllable slip, weight transfer. Setup vocabulary (steering throw, gyro, CS angle) is alien to racing classes.
disciplines.notes: FORGOTTEN: large and growing scene; judged, not timed — different advice model.

disciplines.name: Mini-Z / 1/27-1/28 / 1/24 (small-scale touring, GT, F1)
disciplines.setup_relevance: Tiny chassis: motor pinion/rollout, tyre compound/diameter, front spring, ride height and tweak on smooth surfaces; massive in Japan/Asia. Separate RWD drift sub-scene at 1/24/1/28.
disciplines.notes: FORGOTTEN: huge Asian/club scene across racing AND drift at micro scale.

disciplines.name: 1/10 rally (rally-block tyre touring)
disciplines.setup_relevance: Touring chassis with rally-block tyres and raised ride height on loose surface: tyre and ride-height/suspension travel dominate; a mixed-grip surface case touring setup tools don't cover.
disciplines.notes: FORGOTTEN: loose-surface on-road-derived class.

disciplines.name: 1/8 rallycross / rally game
disciplines.setup_relevance: 1/8 buggy/RG platform on mixed rally terrain; suspension travel and tyre for jumps + loose grip. Niche, mostly basher-adjacent but raced regionally.
disciplines.notes: Under-covered niche; partly basher overlap.

disciplines.name: 1/7 desert / trophy truck (UDR, Felony, Mojave) racing
disciplines.setup_relevance: Heavy long-travel 4WD desert trucks (Traxxas UDR, Arrma Mojave/Felony): shock/spring for big-G landings and high-speed stability. Mostly BASHING with informal speed-run/desert racing — not a sanctioned race class.
disciplines.notes: MOSTLY BASHING, not sanctioned racing — include only as adjacent/aspirational, do NOT treat as a competition class.

disciplines.name: Basher-derived spec classes (Slash spec, AE Reflex/Granite spec, RTR-spec)
disciplines.setup_relevance: Entry classes built around a locked RTR platform (e.g. spec Slash short-course): everything but tyres/shock-oil frozen, so advice is intentionally narrow. The bridge between bashing and real racing.
disciplines.notes: Under-covered: the on-ramp class many real racers start in; spec rules sharply constrain valid advice.

surfaces.name: High-bite clay (groomed/sugared)
surfaces.setup_implications: Traction-roll risk: stiffer shock oil/thicker, taller ride height, wider track, softer-edge tyres; sway bars to control roll. Grip rises as the track grooms in and falls when it dries.

surfaces.name: Hard-packed / blue-groove (dry-slick)
surfaces.setup_implications: Mechanical grip hunting: softer springs/oil, more side-bite tyres, lower ride height; small line/throttle changes matter more than chassis. A single track moves from clay-grip to blue-groove during the day.

surfaces.name: Loamy / loose dirt (outdoor)
surfaces.setup_implications: Maximize forward bite: softer setup, more aggressive/taller tyre pins, more droop; rutted late-race needs ride-height/anti-squat for jumps out of ruts.

surfaces.name: Astroturf (indoor artificial turf / EOS carpet)
surfaces.setup_implications: Glue-grip on tyres, stiffer chassis, anti-roll bars, kit 'high-grip' baseline; traction roll is the enemy. Totally different tyre inserts/compounds than dirt.

surfaces.name: Carpet (off-road and on-road)
surfaces.setup_implications: Stiffest setups, low ride height, ARBs, foam/glued tyres on-road; rollout/gearing precise. Off-road carpet (EOS) needs its own tyre kit and is unforgiving of CG height.

surfaces.name: Asphalt / rubber-laid (on-road)
surfaces.grip_level: high (rises as rubber is laid down through the weekend)
surfaces.setup_implications: Tyre additive/compound, ride height, camber/toe, roll centres; grip evolves with track temp and rubber line. Foam vs rubber tyre choice is class-dependent.

surfaces.name: Banked / flat oval (paved or carpet)
surfaces.setup_implications: Left-only loading: left-side weight bias, tyre stagger, asymmetric ride height/sway-bar, wedge/cross-weight — an asymmetric setup paradigm RaceLab's symmetric tools don't express.

surfaces.name: Dirt/clay oval (left-turn)
surfaces.grip_level: varies (tacky to dry-slick across a session)
surfaces.setup_implications: Rear/tyre stagger, left-weight bias, wedge, sail-panel/wing angle; the track 'takes rubber/moisture' and changes line, so mid-event re-tuning is the norm.

surfaces.name: Indoor vs outdoor (lighting, temp, dust, wind)
surfaces.grip_level: modifier on all of the above
surfaces.setup_implications: Indoor = stable temp/grip, dust control; outdoor = sun-baked grip swings, wind on light pan cars, moisture/dew at dawn/dusk. The SAME class needs different setups indoor vs out.

surfaces.name: Loose gravel / mixed-surface (rally, rallycross)
surfaces.setup_implications: Raised ride height, long travel, rally-block tyres, robust diffs; setup must survive surface transitions within one lap.

surfaces.name: Smooth indoor (drift) / polished tile (Mini-Z)
surfaces.setup_implications: Drift: low-grip rear tyres, gyro gain, counter-steer angle. Mini-Z racing: tyre compound/diameter and tweak on glass-smooth grip — neither maps to RaceLab's classes.

power_subclasses.name: Stock / spec brushless — 17.5T blinky
power_subclasses.applies_to: 1/10 2WD/4WD buggy, stadium truck, SCT, touring car (US stock), some F1
power_subclasses.setup_implications: Flat, low powerband: setup chases corner speed and rotation, precise gearing/rollout, and tyre management — NOT power-down. Blinky (non-timing) ESC forbids boost, so motor timing is not a lever.

power_subclasses.name: Stock / spec brushless — 21.5T / 25.5T blinky
power_subclasses.setup_implications: Even lower power: minimize drag, optimize rollout, light/efficient drivetrain; chassis tweak and tyre are nearly the whole game.

power_subclasses.name: Stock / spec brushless — 13.5T
power_subclasses.applies_to: 1/10 TC stock (EU/ETS), some oval/SCT spec, Mudboss (13.5)
power_subclasses.setup_implications: More power than 17.5 but still capped/blinky in many rules: gearing and traction-on-throttle balance; setup must avoid wheelspin out of slow corners.

power_subclasses.name: Modified brushless (boosted/timing ESC)
power_subclasses.applies_to: 1/10 TC mod, 1/10 off-road mod, 1/12 mod, 1/8 e-buggy/e-truggy
power_subclasses.setup_implications: Open turn (4.5T-8.5T) + boost/turbo timing adds MOTOR tuning (timing/boost curve, rotor, gearing/temp) as a real setup lever alongside chassis; power-down and traction management dominate.

power_subclasses.name: Nitro (.12/.21/.28 glow)
power_subclasses.setup_implications: Adds engine/clutch/needle/pipe/fuel tuning as a parallel domain to chassis — but D13: RaceLab REFUSES engine/nitro tuning advice, so only the clutch-as-chassis-coupling and fuel-load weight effects are in scope.

power_subclasses.name: Gas (23-30cc 2-stroke, large scale)
power_subclasses.setup_implications: Heavy engine + big brakes: brake balance, clutch engagement, and mass management dominate; falls under the same engine-tuning refusal boundary.

power_subclasses.name: RTR-locked spec power
power_subclasses.applies_to: basher-derived spec classes, Mudboss, spec Slash
power_subclasses.setup_implications: Motor/ESC frozen by rule: advice must stay inside the tiny legal window (tyres, shock oil, ride height) — over-recommending illegal mods is the failure mode.

forgotten_or_undercovered: DIRT/CLAY OVAL is an entire missing sub-domain (sprint car, late model, dirt-mod, midget/EDM, legends, Mudboss): asymmetric left-weight-bias + tyre/rear stagger + wedge setup has zero analog in RaceLab's symmetric-track classes — biggest single gap.
PAVED/CARPET OVAL (banked + stagger + cross-weight) is a second asymmetric setup paradigm RaceLab can't express at all.
1/8 e-truggy is absent even though RaceLab already has nitro truggy + e-buggy vocabulary to compose it from — cheapest gap to close.
1/10 4WD short course (4WD SCT) vs 2WD SCT — RaceLab lists 'short course truck' generically; 4WD SCT is a separate setup problem (centre diff, more push).
1/10 World GT / GT12 (WGT pan) is conflated-away under '1/12 electric pan' — different body, weight (750g/1025g) and ride-height window; huge UK/EU grassroots class.
M-chassis / mini touring — large budget club class with short-wheelbase high-CG geometry distinct from full TC.
Vintage/spec on-road (USVTA Trans-Am, 25.5T spec) — one of the biggest North-American spec communities; locked rules sharply constrain legal advice.
RWD competitive drift — judged (not timed) discipline with counter-steer/gyro/Ackermann setup language entirely foreign to RaceLab; growing fast.
Mini-Z / 1/24 / 1/28 micro racing AND micro drift — massive Asian/club scene at a scale RaceLab doesn't touch.
1/10 rally + 1/8 rallycross (loose/mixed surface, rally-block tyres, raised ride height) — loose-grip on-road-derived setups unmodeled.

SURFACE AXIS is the highest-leverage gap WITHIN classes RaceLab already 'covers': the same 1/10 buggy needs radically different setups on loamy dirt vs high-bite clay vs astroturf vs carpet, and the same touring car differs on asphalt vs carpet. Advice that ignores surface is wrong even for covered chassis.

POWER SUB-CLASS AXIS (stock/blinky 17.5T/21.5T/25.5T vs modified/boosted vs RTR-locked spec): stock setup chases corner-speed and rollout while modified setup chases power-down and adds motor-timing as a lever — same chassis, divergent advice. RaceLab labels 'stock + modified' for touring but must enforce this divergence (and the legal-window limits of spec classes) across ALL classes.
INDOOR vs OUTDOOR and time-of-day grip change (dew/sun-bake/track rubbering-in) is a cross-cutting modifier the advisor should reason about for every class, not just weather temp.
eGT (electric 1/8 GT) — new IFMAR title; RaceLab covers nitro IC GT but should flag the electric variant explicitly.
Basher-derived spec classes (spec Slash, RTR-spec) are the on-ramp many real racers start in; under-covered, and demand advice constrained to a frozen platform.

1/7 desert (UDR/Felony/Mojave) and 1/6 trucks are MOSTLY BASHING, not sanctioned racing — correctly low priority, but worth an explicit 'not a race class' note so they aren't mistaken for a coverage gap.
